description: How people live together: trust, exchange, law, conflict, and the economics of scarcity. Sensitive subjects are described with context and care.

concepts.title: Conflict
concepts.summary: The same needs that make us cooperate also set us against each other. Conflict is often what it looks like when two reasonable stories about what's fair collide.

concepts.title: Negotiation
concepts.summary: Working out a deal between people who want different things. The best outcomes come from finding what each side cares about most, since it's rarely the same thing.

concepts.title: Self and Group
concepts.summary: What I need and what we need are rarely identical. A lot of human life is negotiating between the two, again and again, without ever reaching a final answer.

concepts.title: Trust
concepts.summary: Deciding to rely on someone before you can check. Trust makes cooperation cheap and betrayal costly, and it builds slowly through small proofs until a single lapse can undo it.

concepts.title: Trade
concepts.summary: Exchange that leaves both sides better off, which is a stranger fact than it sounds. Trade lets people specialize, spreads ideas along with goods, and ties strangers together in ways no one designed.

concepts.title: Money
concepts.summary: A shared story about what something is worth. Coins, paper, and numbers on a screen all work only because enough people agree that they do.

concepts.title: Markets
concepts.summary: Places, physical or not, where buyers and sellers meet. Prices carry information about what is scarce and what is wanted, coordinating millions of decisions no one is in charge of.

concepts.title: Scarcity
concepts.summary: There is never enough of everything wanted. Economics starts from that, and it's the human-scale echo of entropy: usable energy and attention run out, and we have to choose.

concepts.title: Economics
concepts.summary: The study of how people choose under scarcity. It's part mathematics and part history of human behavior, and it works better on averages than on any single person.

concepts.title: Law
concepts.summary: Rules a society agrees to enforce. They let strangers predict each other and settle disputes without violence, and they carry the values, and the blind spots, of whoever wrote them.

concepts.title: Justice
concepts.summary: The idea that people should get what they're due, and that like cases should be treated alike. What is due, and who decides, is where the arguments live.

concepts.title: Human Rights
concepts.summary: Claims that every person holds simply by being one. They limit what those in power may do, and they are a modern idea that is still being argued into practice.

concepts.title: Government
concepts.summary: The organization that makes and enforces rules for a whole society. Its authority rests on some mix of consent, custom, and force, and much of politics is about the balance.

concepts.title: Education
concepts.summary: How a society passes on what it knows. At its best it helps people learn to think for themselves; at its worst it teaches them what to think.

concepts.title: The Commons
concepts.summary: Resources shared by a community, from pastures to knowledge. They can be quietly ruined by overuse or sustained for generations, depending on the rules people build around them.
